extracted.intended_audience: aviation stakeholders and public commenters (pilots, operators, manufacturers, safety advocates, and others wishing to comment on FAA NPRMs)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for locating FAA proposed rules (NPRMs) and preparing effective comments to the FAA rulemaking docket, including procedural requirements and substantive evidence/formatting expectations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Locate proposed rules on regulations.gov
rubrics_metrics.description: You can find FAA proposed regulations (NPRM) currently available for comment in the Federal Docket Management System at regulations.gov.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Search regulations.gov for the FAA docket for the specific proposed rule you want to comment on; use the docket to view supporting materials and the official text of the NPRM.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submit comments through the Federal eRulemaking Portal (regulations.gov)
rubrics_metrics.description: Comments can be submitted through the Federal eRulemaking Portal at https://www.regulations.gov/ and by following the online instructions for sending your comments electronically. Reference the specific docket number assigned to the proposed rule.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When submitting, follow the portal's instructions, include the docket number so your comment is associated with the correct rulemaking, and use the portal’s commenting features (attachments, supporting documents) as appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not submit sensitive security information to the public docket
rubrics_metrics.description: You should not submit sensitive security information to the rulemaking docket, unless you are invited to do so in the request for comments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the FAA asks for sensitive security information, they will tell you how to submit it and will provide a separate non-public docket. Do not include SSI in public comments to avoid disclosure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cite specific FAA regulations (14 CFR parts)
rubrics_metrics.description: Cite specific FAA regulations (14 CFR Parts 21, 25, 91, 121, 135, etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When arguing about regulatory compliance or proposed changes, reference the exact CFR parts and sections implicated by the proposal to make your comment precise and actionable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Address impacts on pilots, operators, and manufacturers
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe how the proposed rule will affect day-to-day operations, training, maintenance, operational procedures, or design/manufacturing processes for the relevant stakeholders.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide safety data with verifiable sources
rubrics_metrics.description: Include safety data with verifiable sources (NTSB reports, ASRS, etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Support assertions with referenced, authoritative data—e.g., NTSB accident reports, FAA/industry databases, ASRS reports—and provide citations or attachments so reviewers can verify claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Engage with FAA Advisory Circulars and Orders
rubrics_metrics.description: Engage with FAA Advisory Circulars and Orders.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reference relevant Advisory Circulars (ACs) and FAA Orders to show how current guidance or procedures interact with the proposed regulatory change and to ground recommendations in existing FAA guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reference international aviation standards
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When applicable, compare the proposed FAA approach to international standards (ICAO, EASA) to highlight harmonization issues, divergences, or best practices from other jurisdictions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide cost estimates for affected segments
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide cost estimates for affected segments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Quantify economic impacts where possible—costs to operators, manufacturers, training, retrofits—so the FAA can weigh benefits against costs; document assumptions and calculation methods.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distinguish impacts across different operator categories
rubrics_metrics.description: Distinguish impacts on commercial operators, GA, UAS, manufacturers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify and separate effects on commercial airlines, general aviation (GA), unmanned aircraft systems (UAS), and manufacturers rather than making one-size-fits-all statements; explain differing burdens or benefits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use AC 11-2A for participation guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: AC 11-2A provides information on participation in FAA rulemaking.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consult AC 11-2A for procedural guidance on engaging in FAA rulemaking, including recommended practices for submitting comments and participating in the process.

rubrics_metrics.name: Engage with Aviation Rulemaking Committees (ARCs) pre-NPRM
rubrics_metrics.description: Aviation Rulemaking Committees (ARCs) provide pre-NPRM input opportunities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where applicable, participate in ARCs to provide technical or stakeholder input earlier in the rule development process before an NPRM is published.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use ARAC for formal advisory input
rubrics_metrics.description: The Aviation Rulemaking Advisory Committee (ARAC) is the formal advisory body.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider engaging with ARAC channels for formal advisory input on rulemaking topics that fall under ARAC’s remit; ARAC can influence the FAA's rulemaking priorities and technical approaches.

rubrics_metrics.name: Be aware of compressed comment timing for airworthiness directives
rubrics_metrics.description: For airworthiness directives, comment timing is often compressed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When an AD is issued, expect a shorter comment window; prepare to review and submit comments rapidly and prioritize time-sensitive ADs accordingly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Follow distinct processes for special conditions and exemptions
rubrics_metrics.description: Special conditions and exemptions follow distinct comment processes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recognize that special conditions and exemption requests may not use the standard NPRM docket process and may have different submission instructions or timelines; follow the specific procedures announced for those proceedings.
